newsitem.title: USA: Advanta agrees to drop awards card, for now at least.
newsitem.headline: Advanta agrees to drop awards card, for now at least.

text.p: Advanta Corp. said Thursday it settled legal disputes with MasterCard International and Visa U.S.A. over its credit card that would award users points in American Express Co.'s membership rewards programme.

The two credit card companies had sued Advanta to stop it from offering its "Rewards Accelerator" card, which had enabled users to earn points redeemable in the American Express Membership Rewards programme.
Advanta said Thursday that all suits surrounding the issue had been dropped. None of the parties sought or received any money as part of the settlement, it added.
It also said that as part of the settlement Advanta agreed -- at least for now -- to discontinue offering the Rewards Accelerator card.

"We still hold to our original view that the product was in compliance with the bylaws of both MasterCard and Visa and therefore believe that our antitrust claim had merit," Chief Executive Alex W. "Pete" Hart said in a statement.

"But, rather than test it in a protracted legal action, we will await a decision from the Department of Justice, which, we understand, is forming its own opinion on the subject of anti-competitive activity on the part of the associations."

Advanta, a consumer financial services company based in Spring House, Pa., said it remained a member in good standing in both the MasterCard and Visa associations and continued to enjoy all of the privileges of membership.
The settlement follows a March 27 ruing by a federal judge in San Francisco who dismissed, based on a technicality, Advanta's antitrust complaint against MasterCard and Visa.
The judge told Advanta that it could re-plead its claim within 30 days to overcome the technicality.
However, Advanta instead reached a settlement with both card associations out of court.
Advanta's stock added 25 cents to $23.625 in afternoon trading on the Nasdaq market.
